centaur.name: Centaur — Nature 2025
centaur.why: Learns observed human responses with loss restricted to response tokens. Here the institutional action or authentic answer is the observed target; diplomatic generalization remains untested.

raft.name: RAFT — Zhang et al., 2024
raft.why: Teaches answering from relevant documents while ignoring distractors. Our source-grounded examples adapt its evidence-selection idea, not its entire training recipe.

ca.name: Constitutional AI — Bai et al., 2022
ca.why: Turns prose principles into critiques and corrected responses. Dated policy clauses can guide revisions, but may not determine a unique action.

cc.name: Constitutional Classifiers — Sharma et al., 2025
cc.why: Uses written rules to construct classifier supervision. Our adaptation checks policy support and contradictions; the paper evaluates safety safeguards, not diplomatic choices.

dpo.name: DPO — Rafailov et al., 2023
dpo.why: Learns from chosen/rejected responses to the same prompt. Preference validity still depends on evidence and review.

unbench.name: UNBench — Liang et al., AAAI 2026
unbench.why: Separates proposal, voting and statement tasks. These acquired benchmark samples remain evaluation material, not new training examples.

distill.name: Learning by Distilling Context — Snell et al., 2022
distill.why: A teacher sees extra context and the student learns its answers without that context. This can test internalizing stable policy; changing facts should remain available at inference.

dapt.name: Don’t Stop Pretraining — Gururangan et al., ACL 2020
dapt.why: Studies continued domain/task pretraining. Applying text continuation to modern country personas is an optional ablation, not proof of decision fidelity.

policy_examples.title: Apply policy to a concrete question
policy_examples.origin: Authored conversion of a real record; review candidate
policy_examples.system: Answer as a research simulation of the specified government at the stated policy date. Use the supplied evidence. Distinguish stated policy, recorded action and inference; acknowledge unsupported details. Do not invent private motives or fixed national traits.
policy_examples.context:
Project-authored source summaries:
China's 2021 white paper states that development cooperation should respect countries' chosen development paths and should not involve interference, imposed political conditions or pursuit of political self-interest. This is its stated policy, not independent verification of every project.
The white paper describes cooperation projects as being proposed, agreed and led by recipient countries.
policy_examples.question: A proposed development agreement requires the recipient to change its domestic political system. How does that compare with the white paper's stated approach, and can we infer that every Chinese project complies?
policy_examples.completion: That requirement conflicts with the white paper's stated opposition to political strings and interference in a recipient's chosen development path. It also emphasizes recipient leadership of projects. These are published principles; they do not establish the terms or conduct of every Chinese-financed project. [CHN-development-conditions-2021; CHN-development-recipient-leadership-2021]

China's 2021 white paper states that development cooperation should respect countries' chosen development paths and should not involve interference, imposed political conditions or pursuit of political self-interest. This is its stated policy, not independent verification of every project.
The white paper describes cooperation projects as being proposed, agreed and led by recipient countries.

A proposed development agreement requires the recipient to change its domestic political system. How does that compare with the white paper's stated approach, and can we infer that every Chinese project complies?
